newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Russia consider joint high-tech fund.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Russia consider joint high-tech fund.

text.p: Russia is willing to invest up to $50 million in a proposed fund for joint high-tech projects with Israel, an Israeli industry and trade ministry official said on Tuesday.
An adviser to Gennady Seleznyov, speaker of the State Duma (lower house of parliament), made the offer in a meeting on Monday in Jerusalem with Israeli Industry and Trade Minister Natan Sharansky.
"The minister was astounded by Russia's willingness to invest such a large sum," Volodia Voronel, an adviser to Sharanksy on technological matters, told Reuters.
Voronel said Israel had yet to determine how much it would contribute to the fund "but the minister will try not to disappoint the Russians".
A ministry official will visit Russia soon to sign a memorandum of understanding on establishing the fund.
Voronel said the fund could provide the perfect means by which to link Russia's large number of research laboratories and skilled personnel with Israel's Western marketing experience.
He said the fund, through an administrative company it would set up, would also seek private backing for high-tech projects.
Israel proposed that individuals as well as companies be allowed to present projects for funding, Voronel said.
Annual trade between Israel and Russia now stands at about $500 million.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited Russia earlier this month. Sharansky, a former dissident freed from a Soviet jail in a 1986 East-West spy swap, visited Russia several weeks ago for the first time since immigrating to Israel.
